description: Temporary, expiring acceptances for reviewed Expo developer-tooling advisories. node-forge and braces have no upstream release outside their advisory ranges. source-map-js has a patch that remains inside the repository's seven-day release quarantine until 2026-10-07T14:08:09Z. None of these paths accepts approval traffic, and each entry must be removed when its stated remediation becomes eligible.

exceptions.title: node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements
exceptions.reachability: Developer-machine CLI tooling only, not device-reachable application code. The installed paths are expo 57.0.25 -> @expo/cli 57.0.27 -> node-forge 1.4.0 and @expo/cli 57.0.27 -> @expo/code-signing-certificates 0.0.6 -> node-forge 1.4.0. @expo/cli is the `expo` command binary (expo's package.json bin entry); expo's runtime entry does not import it, no app source imports node-forge, @expo/cli, or @expo/code-signing-certificates, and the deterministic iOS and Android exports contain no node-forge code. Inside the CLI, node-forge RSA verification runs in exactly two places, both in the development-server manifest signer: validateSelfSignedCertificate checks the self-signature of a project's own updates.codeSigningCertificate read from local disk, and signBufferRSASHA256AndVerify re-verifies a signature the CLI has just produced with its own private key. Neither path accepts an attacker-chosen signature as an authorization decision, and both are unreachable here because app.json sets neither updates.codeSigningCertificate nor extra.eas.projectId and expo-updates is not installed. The app's own approval signatures use @noble/curves P-256, not RSA.

no_upstream_fix.how_checked: GitHub advisory GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv lists no first patched version. The npm registry shows node-forge 1.4.0 (2026-03-24) as the latest release and dist-tag. Upstream has no tag after v1.4.0; the fix is the open, unmerged digitalbazaar/forge#1152. Every Expo CLI line checked still depends on node-forge ^1.3.3 and @expo/code-signing-certificates ^0.0.6: @expo/cli 57.0.26, 57.0.27 (latest), 58.1.1 (next), and the 58 canary. @expo/code-signing-certificates 0.0.7 (2026-09-30) only raises its node-forge floor to ^1.4.0, which is still inside the advisory range.
no_upstream_fix.why_suggested_fix_rejected: expo@44.0.6 is thirteen SDK majors behind, predates the bundled @expo/cli, and targets react-native 0.64.3 rather than the pinned 0.86.3; it would trade one unreachable tooling advisory for an unsupported runtime. Overriding node-forge to an unreleased upstream branch would pull unreviewed code into the mobile approval boundary and bypass the seven-day release quarantine.

exceptions.revisit_trigger: When node-forge publishes a release outside <=1.4.0 and it clears this app's seven-day min-release-age, refresh the lock so @expo/cli resolves it through its ^1.3.3 range, require a zero-advisory npm audit, and delete this entry. Revisit immediately if app.json gains updates.codeSigningCertificate or extra.eas.projectId, if expo-updates is added, if any app source imports node-forge or @expo/code-signing-certificates, if an exported bundle contains node-forge, or if severity or affected packages change.

exceptions.title: braces vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns
exceptions.reachability: Bundler and file-watcher tooling on the developer or CI machine only, not device-reachable application code. The single installed copy is braces 3.0.3 under micromatch 4.0.8, reached by expo 57.0.25 -> @expo/cli 57.0.27 -> @expo/metro-file-map 57.0.3 -> micromatch -> braces and by expo -> @expo/metro 56.0.2 -> metro 0.84.5 -> metro-file-map 0.84.5 -> micromatch -> braces; the react-native, @react-native and metro-* entries in the affected set are parents of that same Metro edge, not separate consumers. The only importers of micromatch in the tree are @expo/metro-file-map/build/watchers/common.js and metro-file-map/src/watchers/common.js (includedByGlob), and nothing imports braces directly. braces expands only the pattern argument, never the path being tested, and those patterns are built by the watcher from local Metro configuration: '**/*', '**/package.json', the health-check file prefix, and '**/*.' plus each resolver source extension. File paths come from the local filesystem; nothing derived from approval requests, pairing payloads, receipts or the network reaches a glob. The source maps of fresh iOS and Android `expo export --no-bytecode` bundles list no module from braces, micromatch, metro-file-map or @expo/metro-file-map, and neither bundle contains the strings braces or micromatch. The worst case is a RangeError that aborts a local bundler or watcher run.

no_upstream_fix.npm_suggested_fix: semver-major downgrade to expo@44.0.6 (and react-native@0.72.17 for the Metro edge)
no_upstream_fix.how_checked: GitHub advisory GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm lists no first patched version. The npm registry shows braces 3.0.3 as the latest release and dist-tag, and micromatch 4.0.8 (latest) still depends on braces ^3.0.3. @expo/metro-file-map 57.0.3 (latest) and 58.0.3 (next) and metro-file-map 0.87.1 (latest) all still depend on micromatch ^4.0.4, and @expo/cli 57.0.27 (latest) depends on @expo/metro-file-map ^57.0.3.
no_upstream_fix.why_suggested_fix_rejected: expo@44.0.6 and react-native@0.72.17 are many SDK and React Native majors behind the pinned expo 57.0.25 and react-native 0.86.3; they would trade one build-tool advisory for an unsupported runtime. There is no patched braces or braces-free micromatch to override to, and replacing Metro's watcher dependency with an unreleased fork would pull unreviewed code into the build and bypass the seven-day release quarantine.

exceptions.revisit_trigger: Matches the root audit's BRACES_RECHECK_BY of 2026-12-01 for the same advisory. When braces publishes a release outside <=3.0.3, or micromatch, @expo/metro-file-map and metro-file-map drop braces, and it clears this app's seven-day min-release-age, refresh the lock, require the gate to pass without this entry, and delete it. Revisit immediately if any app source imports braces, micromatch, metro-file-map or @expo/metro-file-map, if an exported bundle contains any of them, if npm reports a new package in this advisory's affected set, or if the severity changes.

exceptions.title: source-map-js event-loop denial of service through indexed source-map section offsets
exceptions.reachability: The single installed source-map-js 1.2.1 copy is reached only through PostCSS under Expo Metro configuration. It processes developer-controlled source maps during local or CI bundling; application code does not import source-map-js, approval requests and receipts cannot supply its inputs, and it is not an authorization decision point. The advisory can therefore abort a build only if a maintainer introduces a hostile source map into the build inputs. The exception is intentionally shorter than two days because the patched 1.2.2 release clears the repository's seven-day supply-chain quarantine on 2026-10-07T14:08:09Z.

no_upstream_fix.how_checked: GitHub advisory GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q names 1.2.2 as patched. npm records 1.2.2 as published at 2026-09-30T14:08:09Z, so it becomes eligible under this repository's seven-day min-release-age policy at 2026-10-07T14:08:09Z. npm explain shows the installed copy only beneath the pinned PostCSS build dependency.
no_upstream_fix.why_suggested_fix_rejected: Installing 1.2.2 before 2026-10-07T14:08:09Z would bypass the repository's deliberate seven-day quarantine for new third-party releases. The one-day acceptance preserves that control and expires immediately after the patch becomes eligible; it does not claim the vulnerable parser is safe for untrusted source maps.

exceptions.revisit_trigger: As soon as 2026-10-07T14:08:09Z passes, pin source-map-js 1.2.2 in the secure-app override, refresh the lockfile, rerun deterministic iOS and Android export checks plus npm audit, and delete this entry. Revisit immediately if application source imports source-map-js, if approval or network data reaches PostCSS source-map parsing, or if npm attributes the advisory to any additional package.
